---
title: "Graphic size and timing"
description: Set the size a graphic draws at, fit it to the canvas, and control how its own animation runs when the clip gets longer, shorter or split.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic is drawn fresh at a size you choose, and it has an animation timeline of its own. The **Size** and **Timeline** sections of the **Graphic** sub-tab set both, so you can make a graphic sharp at any size and decide whether its outro follows the end of the clip.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Timeline']}
  tools={['set_graphic', 'set_video', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
/>

## Width and Height

**Width** and **Height** are the size the graphic draws at, in whole pixels from 1 to 8192 a side. The graphic's code lays itself out at that size, so text and shapes stay sharp.

The **Size** section starts collapsed, and its header shows the size, for example `1920 × 1080`. With several graphic clips selected, a change applies to all of them, and a row shows mixed when they differ.

A new graphic takes the size its module asks for, or the canvas's size if it doesn't ask.

The graphic is drawn at this size and then placed on the canvas like any other layer. Scaling the clip in the [Picture](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab scales that finished picture. To make a graphic bigger and keep it crisp, raise **Width** and **Height** rather than the scale.

Changing the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) never changes a graphic's size. [Make Vertical Version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) is the one exception.

## Fit to Canvas

**Fit to Canvas** in the **Size** section sets the size to the canvas's, then centres the clip at scale 1. It works on every selected graphic clip, as one undo step called Fit Graphic to Canvas.

A graphic can't be larger than 8192 pixels a side, so on a bigger canvas Frame Job tells you why and leaves the clip as it was.

## The graphic's own timeline

A graphic counts its own frames from its first frame, separately from the project's timeline. The **Timeline** section shows where the clip sits on that count. It appears only when one clip is selected, it starts collapsed, and its header shows the length.

| Row | What it shows | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | The graphic frame the clip's first frame shows. | Nothing directly. Trimming the front, rolling the cut before the clip and splitting all move it. |
| **Length** | How long the graphic's own timeline runs. | Type a timecode to pin it. |
| **Follow Clip** | Whether the graphic's timeline ends when the clip ends. | Tick or untick it. |

### Follow Clip

**Follow Clip** is on for a new clip. The graphic's timeline ends with the clip, so when you lengthen the clip its outro moves to the new end. Most graphics want this.

Unticking **Follow Clip** pins **Length** at its current value. Ticking it again hands the length back to the clip.

### Length

Typing in **Length** pins it, which unticks **Follow Clip**, and is one undo step called Graphic Length. A pinned graphic keeps its pace however long the clip gets, so the animation doesn't stretch and its outro stays at the same point.

The value snaps to a frame and can't be less than one frame. Typing the value the field already shows changes nothing, so untick **Follow Clip** to pin the length as it stands.

### Length shorter or longer than the clip

When **Length** is pinned shorter than the clip, the graphic keeps counting frames past it, but its progress stays at the end. What you see depends on how the graphic is written:

- An animation driven by progress holds its end state.
- An animation driven by frame numbers keeps going.

When **Length** is pinned longer than the clip, the clip ends before the graphic's timeline does, so a late outro never plays.

## Trim a graphic like footage

Trimming a graphic clip cuts into its animation, as trimming a video cuts into its footage. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) and [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) work as they do on any clip.

| Edit | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Trim the start, or roll the cut before the clip | **In** moves, so the animation starts further in. **Length** stays the same, so the outro keeps its timing. |
| Trim the end, **Follow Clip** on | The graphic's timeline ends at the clip's new end. |
| Trim the end, **Length** pinned | **Length** doesn't change. Shortening the clip can cut off the outro. |
| Drag the start earlier | A graphic has no source to run out of, so the start can go back as far as the track allows. **In** moves back and stops at 0. |
| [Split](/editing/splitting/) the clip | The second half's **In** moves, so it carries on where the first half left off. Both halves pin **Length** to the original's, which unticks **Follow Clip** on both and keeps the outro at the same point. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | The clip stretches or squeezes like a title. A pinned **Length** stays as it was. |

## Good to know

- Actions can't animate size or timing. With an action selected, the **Size** and **Timeline** sections show ⊘ and always change the clip. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
- Adding a [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) that gives a graphic clip extra frames at its head moves **In** back by the same amount, so the picture stays in step. Where **In** is shorter than the extension it stops at 0, and the graphic's first frame lands on the clip's new first frame.
- Changing the [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) moves a graphic's own timeline onto the new frames. **In** and a pinned **Length** snap to the nearest frame. A graphic that counts in seconds keeps its pace, and one that counts frames runs faster at a higher rate.

## Related

- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
- [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)

---
title: "Graphics in a vertical version"
description: How Make Vertical Version re-sizes and re-lays your graphics for a tall or square canvas, which older template copies it updates, and which modules it names for you to check.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) has to turn a wide layout into a tall or square one, and graphics can lay themselves out again where footage can't. This page says what happens to each graphic, and which ones you might want to look at afterwards.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  tools="make_vertical_version"
/>

## Canvas-sized graphics

A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, each side, is re-sized to the new canvas, so the module lays itself out again on the new frame. This is usually a full-frame lower third or title card. A 1920 × 1080 graphic on a 1920 × 1080 canvas becomes 1080 × 1920 for 9:16.

Its position shrinks and stretches with the two sides of the canvas, and so do the positions its [actions](/graphics/animate-properties/) move it to. Its scale stays as it was, because the graphic is the canvas's size again.

This is the one change of canvas that changes a graphic's size. Everywhere else, [Width and Height](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height) stay as you set them.

## Graphics of any other size

Any other graphic is kept as placed and rescaled from the old canvas, like a title. That includes a graphic with the same area as the canvas but another shape, such as 1080 × 1920 on a 1920 × 1080 canvas.

## Templates measured by the short side

These [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) measure themselves by the canvas's short side, so they fit a tall frame:

- Lower third
- Title card
- Callout
- Bar chart
- Counter
- Kinetic type

They draw exactly as before on a landscape or square canvas.

## Older template copies

A project can hold an older copy of one of those six, inserted before they measured by the short side. Frame Job looks at every module a clip draws, on the timeline and inside nests, and recognises these by their text, never their name. A copy you renamed `intro` is still found.

What happens next depends on **Make a copy** in the sheet:

| **Make a copy** | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Ticked | The copy that opens has each older module rewritten with the current template. Your earlier text is kept as the module's previous version, so [File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…](/graphics/manage-graphics/) brings it back. The project you started from never changes. |
| Unticked | Nothing is rewritten, and the summary names each module. |

## Your own modules

A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height, with `ctx.height / 1080` in its text, is named in the summary, because it may not fit the narrow frame. This applies with or without **Make a copy**, and the module is never rewritten.

A template you've edited counts as your own, since its text no longer matches any template Frame Job shipped.

To fix one of these, measure by the short side instead:

```js
const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
```

On a landscape canvas that's the same number as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a tall canvas drawing the graphic 1.78 times too big. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).

## What the summary says

The sheet's summary reports all of this before you choose **Make**, and it stays accurate as you change the sheet.

| The summary says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Re-sizes 2 graphics to the new canvas." | That many canvas-sized graphics are being re-sized. |
| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | That many older template copies are rewritten in the copy. |
| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." | You've unticked **Make a copy**. Tick it to update the module. |
| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it sizes itself by the canvas's height, so it may not fit the narrow frame." | Check this graphic on the new canvas. |

## Related

- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [What a vertical version changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)

---
title: "Animate graphic properties"
description: Use an action to move a graphic's numbers and colours over time, switch its text and pictures at a set moment, and keep some properties out of the animation.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A graphic's [properties](/graphics/properties/) can change over time, in the same way an [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip's position or fades its opacity. Use this to slide a bar's size, change an accent colour, or swap a line of text part way through a clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, with an action selected"
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_graphic']}
/>

## Animate with an action

<Steps>

1. Select the graphic clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>).

2. With the action selected, open the **Graphic** sub-tab.

3. In **Properties**, set the values the graphic should end at. Each row you change gets a ◆.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the change.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a count of 3. The accent, size and boxed rows have a diamond in their gutter, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
/>

While an action is selected, the **Properties** rows edit the action's end, not the clip. A value you set is kept as you set it, even when it equals the module's default. **Size** and **Timeline** always edit the clip, and they show ⊘.

The graphic gets the current values on every frame, and any animation the module does for itself still runs on top.

To stop animating a property, take it out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action).

## What ramps

Numbers and colours move along the action's curve from start to end.

**A number** arrives with decimals. Going from 64 to 129, it's 96.5 halfway, and it's never rounded or snapped to the property's step.

**A colour** blends through OKLab, which keeps the middle of the blend clean, and its transparency blends as a separate value. `#ff0000` to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, and `#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, a half-transparent grey.

While a property moves, every frame has to be drawn anew. A graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

:::caution
A module that needs whole numbers has to round them itself, or mark the property [`animate: false`](#stop-a-property-animating). One that does neither can fail on a fraction. Those frames draw the error card, and an export stops there.
:::

## What switches

Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures can't blend. They hold their value through the action, then change to the end's value as the action ends. Their rows say "at end".

An action starts from the value in force when it begins. That's the clip's own value, or what an earlier action finished on.

A module can mark any property with `animate: false`, and no action will ever animate it. Modules use this for a count, a layout mode or a data series, where a value part way between two others would break the drawing.

};

- If an action names a property the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate, the row shows dimmed with **⌫**. Choose it to take the property out of the action.

---
title: "Paste Graphic Properties"
description: Copy the text, colours and other properties of one graphic clip onto other clips drawn by the same graphic, and see what stays behind.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Paste Graphic Properties copies what one graphic clip shows, its text and colours included, onto other clips drawn by the same graphic. Use it to give a run of lower thirds the same styling, then change the names.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties"
  tools="paste_attributes"
/>

## Paste graphic properties

<Steps>

1. Select the graphic clip you want to copy from and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips to paste onto.

3. Choose **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

</Steps>

Every selected clip drawn by the same graphic takes the copied properties, as one undo step. The menu item is on when there are Frame Job clips on the clipboard and at least one graphic clip is selected.

## What moves and what stays

The target ends up with exactly the copied clip's properties, so a property left at its default on the copied clip goes back to the default on the target.

Each target keeps:

- Its own module, size, **In** and **Length**.
- Its position, scale and everything else outside the **Properties** section.
- Any property the copied clip leaves unset and an action on the target animates, so that the action keeps its start.

If you copied several clips, only the earliest one is read.

## When it does nothing

| What you'll see | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Some selected clips don't change | They're drawn by another graphic, or they aren't graphics. They're skipped. |
| A beep | The copied clip isn't a graphic, no selected clip is drawn by the same graphic, or the targets already match. |
| An alert | The copied properties can't be stored, for example more than 64 of them. It gives the reason, and nothing changes. |

## How it differs from Paste Attributes

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) copies a clip's look, such as its position and opacity, and never carries graphic properties. The two are separate on purpose, because a graphic's properties hold its words as well as its look.

| | Paste Attributes | Paste Graphic Properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position, scale, opacity and other picture settings | Yes | No |
| A graphic's text, colours and other properties | No | Yes |

See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

## Copying a graphic clip

Copying and pasting a graphic clip (<kbd>⌘C</kbd>, <kbd>⌘V</kbd>) pastes a clip that names its module. The module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied.

So in another project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card. To fix it, add the module under the same name, for example with **From File…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** on a file of that name. **From File…** also places a clip of its own, which you can delete.

See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).

## With an agent

An agent uses `paste_attributes` and has to ask for the graphic group by name, since it's never part of the default set. Unlike the menu item, a clip drawn by another graphic stops the paste with an error, unless the agent asks to skip those. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)

---
title: "Fonts and pictures in graphics"
description: Add fonts and pictures to a project's graphics, find the exact font name a graphic must use, and see why a font or picture doesn't draw.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic draws only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the fonts and pictures you add to the project, so it looks the same on any Mac. This page covers adding them, and what to do when one doesn't draw.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…', 'File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…']}
  tools={['import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'get_graphic']}
/>

## Add a font

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. Pick a `.ttf` or `.otf` file.

</Steps>

Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` folder, and every graphic in the project can then use it, straight away. Nothing is shown when it works.

A file with the same name replaces the old one. If the file holds no font Frame Job can load, an alert says so and nothing is added.

## Use the exact family name

The family name a graphic must use is the one the graphics engine reads from the file. It can differ from the name Font Book or other apps show.

If a font doesn't draw, select the clip and open **Source** in the **Graphic** sub-tab. Under "Checked at the clip's first frame" it reports the missing family and lists every family the project has, so you can copy the exact name from there. The section's header shows "1 warning" when there's something to read.

The check looks at the clip's first frame only, so a font used later in the animation isn't reported there.

## Bundled fonts

These seven families draw on every Mac, with nothing to install.

| Family | Weights |
| --- | --- |
| Anton | 400 |
| Bebas Neue | 400 |
| Darker Grotesque | Variable, 300 to 900 |
| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
| Source Sans 3 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
| Source Serif 4 | Variable, 200 to 900 |

## Generic families

A module can also ask for a generic family, which draws in a bundled face.

| Generic | Draws in |
| --- | --- |
| `serif` | Source Serif 4 |
| `sans-serif` | Source Sans 3 |
| `monospace` | IBM Plex Mono |

Write a generic without quotes, as in `font-family="sans-serif"`. With quotes it names a family called "sans-serif", which isn't there. `cursive` and `fantasy` aren't available.

## System fonts

Graphics never use the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere. To use one of them, add its file to the project with [Add Font to Graphics](#add-a-font).

What happens to a family name in a module:

- A family the project doesn't have draws nothing, with a warning naming the families it does have.
- In a list such as `"Nope, Montserrat"`, the first family the project has draws.
- A family with a word starting with a digit must be quoted, as in `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`. Unquoted, it draws nothing, with a warning.

:::note
[Text clips](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) work differently, and do use the fonts on your Mac.
:::

## Add a picture

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. Pick a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file.

</Steps>

Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/assets/` folder. A module can then draw it, and a [picture property's](/graphics/properties/) pop-up lists it.

A file with the same name replaces the old one. An empty file is refused with an alert, and so is any other kind of file.

## Picture names

A module refers to a picture by its file name, and some names can't be used that way. A name is not usable when it:

- Starts with `.` or `#`.
- Holds any of `/ : " ' < > &`, or a control character.
- Is longer than 247 bytes.

A picture with a name like that is added under a legal one, and a notice tells you which: "#logo&mark.png" was added as "logo-mark.png": asset(name) cannot use the name it had.

If the legal name is taken, the picture takes `-2`, `-3` and so on, as in `logo-mark-2.png`. A renamed copy never replaces an existing file.

## Drop files in the folder

You can also put fonts and pictures straight into `graphics/fonts/` and `graphics/assets/` with the Finder or any other tool. Frame Job notices within a moment.

To find the folder, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the **Source** section of a graphic clip. It shows the module's file inside `graphics/`. If `fonts` or `assets` isn't there yet, make a folder with exactly that name.

Anything the folder scan can't use is skipped, with a warning in **Source** under "In the graphics folder":

- A font that doesn't load.
- An empty picture.
- A picture with a name a module can't use. Unlike a picture added from the menu, it isn't renamed for you.

## Good to know

- Neither import is an undo step. To take a file out, delete it from the folder.
- Fonts and pictures belong to the project. Another project needs its own copy.
- Both menu items work as soon as the project window is open. There's no need to save first.

## With an agent

An agent can read the exact family names directly, rather than waiting for a warning. `get_graphic` lists them, and `import_graphic_font` answers with the names a new file adds. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

## Related

- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
- [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/)

```

---
title: "Graphic size and timing"
description: Set the size a graphic draws at, fit it to the canvas, and control how its own animation runs when the clip gets longer, shorter or split.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic is drawn fresh at a size you choose, and it has an animation timeline of its own. The **Size** and **Timeline** sections of the **Graphic** sub-tab set both, so you can make a graphic sharp at any size and decide whether its outro follows the end of the clip.

<AtAGlance
  where={['Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Size', 'Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Timeline']}
  tools={['set_graphic', 'set_video', 'trim_start', 'trim_end', 'roll']}
/>

## Width and Height

**Width** and **Height** are the size the graphic draws at, in whole pixels from 1 to 8192 a side. The graphic's code lays itself out at that size, so text and shapes stay sharp.

The **Size** section starts collapsed, and its header shows the size, for example `1920 × 1080`. With several graphic clips selected, a change applies to all of them, and a row shows mixed when they differ.

A new graphic takes the size its module asks for, or the canvas's size if it doesn't ask.

The graphic is drawn at this size and then placed on the canvas like any other layer. Scaling the clip in the [Picture](/canvas/picture-tab/) sub-tab scales that finished picture. To make a graphic bigger and keep it crisp, raise **Width** and **Height** rather than the scale.

Changing the [canvas size](/projects/canvas-size/) never changes a graphic's size. [Make Vertical Version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/) is the one exception.

## Fit to Canvas

**Fit to Canvas** in the **Size** section sets the size to the canvas's, then centres the clip at scale 1. It works on every selected graphic clip, as one undo step called Fit Graphic to Canvas.

A graphic can't be larger than 8192 pixels a side, so on a bigger canvas Frame Job tells you why and leaves the clip as it was.

## The graphic's own timeline

A graphic counts its own frames from its first frame, separately from the project's timeline. The **Timeline** section shows where the clip sits on that count. It appears only when one clip is selected, it starts collapsed, and its header shows the length.

| Row | What it shows | What you can do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **In** | The graphic frame the clip's first frame shows. | Nothing directly. Trimming the front, rolling the cut before the clip and splitting all move it. |
| **Length** | How long the graphic's own timeline runs. | Type a timecode to pin it. |
| **Follow Clip** | Whether the graphic's timeline ends when the clip ends. | Tick or untick it. |

### Follow Clip

**Follow Clip** is on for a new clip. The graphic's timeline ends with the clip, so when you lengthen the clip its outro moves to the new end. Most graphics want this.

Unticking **Follow Clip** pins **Length** at its current value. Ticking it again hands the length back to the clip.

### Length

Typing in **Length** pins it, which unticks **Follow Clip**, and is one undo step called Graphic Length. A pinned graphic keeps its pace however long the clip gets, so the animation doesn't stretch and its outro stays at the same point.

The value snaps to a frame and can't be less than one frame. Typing the value the field already shows changes nothing, so untick **Follow Clip** to pin the length as it stands.

### Length shorter or longer than the clip

When **Length** is pinned shorter than the clip, the graphic keeps counting frames past it, but its progress stays at the end. What you see depends on how the graphic is written:

- An animation driven by progress holds its end state.
- An animation driven by frame numbers keeps going.

When **Length** is pinned longer than the clip, the clip ends before the graphic's timeline does, so a late outro never plays.

## Trim a graphic like footage

Trimming a graphic clip cuts into its animation, as trimming a video cuts into its footage. [Trim](/editing/trimming/) and [roll](/editing/slip-and-roll/) work as they do on any clip.

| Edit | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Trim the start, or roll the cut before the clip | **In** moves, so the animation starts further in. **Length** stays the same, so the outro keeps its timing. |
| Trim the end, **Follow Clip** on | The graphic's timeline ends at the clip's new end. |
| Trim the end, **Length** pinned | **Length** doesn't change. Shortening the clip can cut off the outro. |
| Drag the start earlier | A graphic has no source to run out of, so the start can go back as far as the track allows. **In** moves back and stops at 0. |
| [Split](/editing/splitting/) the clip | The second half's **In** moves, so it carries on where the first half left off. Both halves pin **Length** to the original's, which unticks **Follow Clip** on both and keeps the outro at the same point. |
| [Retime Range](/speed/retime-range/) | The clip stretches or squeezes like a title. A pinned **Length** stays as it was. |

## Good to know

- Actions can't animate size or timing. With an action selected, the **Size** and **Timeline** sections show ⊘ and always change the clip. See [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/).
- Adding a [transition](/motion/add-a-transition/) that gives a graphic clip extra frames at its head moves **In** back by the same amount, so the picture stays in step. Where **In** is shorter than the extension it stops at 0, and the graphic's first frame lands on the clip's new first frame.
- Changing the [project frame rate](/projects/frame-rate/) moves a graphic's own timeline onto the new frames. **In** and a pinned **Length** snap to the nearest frame. A graphic that counts in seconds keeps its pace, and one that counts frames runs faster at a higher rate.

## Related

- [The Graphic sub-tab](/graphics/graphic-tab/)
- [Animate graphic properties](/graphics/animate-properties/)
- [Graphics in a vertical version](/graphics/vertical-graphics/)
- [Trim clips](/editing/trimming/)

---
title: "Graphics in a vertical version"
description: How Make Vertical Version re-sizes and re-lays your graphics for a tall or square canvas, which older template copies it updates, and which modules it names for you to check.
---

import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

[Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/) has to turn a wide layout into a tall or square one, and graphics can lay themselves out again where footage can't. This page says what happens to each graphic, and which ones you might want to look at afterwards.

<AtAGlance
  menu="File ▸ Make Vertical Version…"
  tools="make_vertical_version"
/>

## Canvas-sized graphics

A graphic exactly the old canvas's size, each side, is re-sized to the new canvas, so the module lays itself out again on the new frame. This is usually a full-frame lower third or title card. A 1920 × 1080 graphic on a 1920 × 1080 canvas becomes 1080 × 1920 for 9:16.

Its position shrinks and stretches with the two sides of the canvas, and so do the positions its [actions](/graphics/animate-properties/) move it to. Its scale stays as it was, because the graphic is the canvas's size again.

This is the one change of canvas that changes a graphic's size. Everywhere else, [Width and Height](/graphics/size-and-timing/#width-and-height) stay as you set them.

## Graphics of any other size

Any other graphic is kept as placed and rescaled from the old canvas, like a title. That includes a graphic with the same area as the canvas but another shape, such as 1080 × 1920 on a 1920 × 1080 canvas.

## Templates measured by the short side

These [bundled templates](/graphics/templates/) measure themselves by the canvas's short side, so they fit a tall frame:

- Lower third
- Title card
- Callout
- Bar chart
- Counter
- Kinetic type

They draw exactly as before on a landscape or square canvas.

## Older template copies

A project can hold an older copy of one of those six, inserted before they measured by the short side. Frame Job looks at every module a clip draws, on the timeline and inside nests, and recognises these by their text, never their name. A copy you renamed `intro` is still found.

What happens next depends on **Make a copy** in the sheet:

| **Make a copy** | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Ticked | The copy that opens has each older module rewritten with the current template. Your earlier text is kept as the module's previous version, so [File ▸ Restore Graphic Version…](/graphics/manage-graphics/) brings it back. The project you started from never changes. |
| Unticked | Nothing is rewritten, and the summary names each module. |

## Your own modules

A module of your own that sizes itself by the canvas's height, with `ctx.height / 1080` in its text, is named in the summary, because it may not fit the narrow frame. This applies with or without **Make a copy**, and the module is never rewritten.

A template you've edited counts as your own, since its text no longer matches any template Frame Job shipped.

To fix one of these, measure by the short side instead:

```js
const u = Math.min(ctx.width, ctx.height) / 1080;
```

On a landscape canvas that's the same number as `ctx.height / 1080`, and it stops a tall canvas drawing the graphic 1.78 times too big. See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/).

## What the summary says

The sheet's summary reports all of this before you choose **Make**, and it stays accurate as you change the sheet.

| The summary says | What it means |
| --- | --- |
| "Re-sizes 2 graphics to the new canvas." | That many canvas-sized graphics are being re-sized. |
| "Updates 1 graphic module to the current template." | That many older template copies are rewritten in the copy. |
| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it is an older copy of the bundled template "lower-third"; Make Vertical updates it only in a copy." | You've unticked **Make a copy**. Tick it to update the module. |
| "Graphic module "intro" is left as it is: it sizes itself by the canvas's height, so it may not fit the narrow frame." | Check this graphic on the new canvas. |

## Related

- [Make Vertical Version](/framing/make-vertical-version/)
- [What a vertical version changes](/framing/vertical-what-changes/)
- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)
- [Rename, delete and restore graphics](/graphics/manage-graphics/)

---
title: "Animate graphic properties"
description: Use an action to move a graphic's numbers and colours over time, switch its text and pictures at a set moment, and keep some properties out of the animation.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

A graphic's [properties](/graphics/properties/) can change over time, in the same way an [action](/motion/actions/) moves a clip's position or fades its opacity. Use this to slide a bar's size, change an accent colour, or swap a line of text part way through a clip.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Clip ▸ Add Action"
  keys="⌥⌘K"
  where="Clip tab ▸ Graphic ▸ Properties, with an action selected"
  tools={['add_action', 'set_action_end', 'set_graphic']}
/>

## Animate with an action

<Steps>

1. Select the graphic clip, move the playhead to where the change should start, and choose **Clip ▸ Add Action** (<kbd>⌥⌘K</kbd>).

2. With the action selected, open the **Graphic** sub-tab.

3. In **Properties**, set the values the graphic should end at. Each row you change gets a ◆.

4. Move the playhead through the action, or play it, to see the change.

</Steps>

<Shot
  name="07b-clip-graphic-action.inspector"
  alt="The Clip tab with action 1 selected on a graphic clip. The Graphic sub-tab and the Properties section each show a count of 3. The accent, size and boxed rows have a diamond in their gutter, and boxed says at end. The Size and Timeline sections show the ⊘ mark."
/>

While an action is selected, the **Properties** rows edit the action's end, not the clip. A value you set is kept as you set it, even when it equals the module's default. **Size** and **Timeline** always edit the clip, and they show ⊘.

The graphic gets the current values on every frame, and any animation the module does for itself still runs on top.

To stop animating a property, take it out of the action. See [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/#take-a-property-out-of-the-action).

## What ramps

Numbers and colours move along the action's curve from start to end.

**A number** arrives with decimals. Going from 64 to 129, it's 96.5 halfway, and it's never rounded or snapped to the property's step.

**A colour** blends through OKLab, which keeps the middle of the blend clean, and its transparency blends as a separate value. `#ff0000` to `#0000ff` is `#8c53a2` halfway, and `#ffffff` to `#00000000` is `#63636380`, a half-transparent grey.

While a property moves, every frame has to be drawn anew. A graphic that had settled costs a full draw per frame for the length of the action. See [Graphics playback and memory](/graphics/playback-and-memory/).

:::caution
A module that needs whole numbers has to round them itself, or mark the property [`animate: false`](#stop-a-property-animating). One that does neither can fail on a fraction. Those frames draw the error card, and an export stops there.
:::

## What switches

Text, checkboxes, pop-ups and pictures can't blend. They hold their value through the action, then change to the end's value as the action ends. Their rows say "at end".

For a picture, choosing **None** in the pop-up means no picture from the end of the action.

## Where an animated property starts

An action starts from the value in force when it begins. That's the clip's own value, or what an earlier action finished on.

If the clip holds no value for a property, the first action to name it starts from the module's default at that moment. That default is written into the clip in the same undo step, so changing the default later doesn't move the animation.

Resetting the clip's own value for a property an action animates sets it to the default, so the action still has somewhere to start from.

## Stop a property animating

A module can mark any property with `animate: false`, and no action will ever animate it. Modules use this for a count, a layout mode or a data series, where a value part way between two others would break the drawing.

The property's row shows ⊘, and it edits the clip even while an action is selected.

If you write modules, it's one more key on the schema entry. It must be `true` or `false`, and anything else stops the module compiling. Leaving it out means `true`.

```js
export const schema = {
  count: { type: "number", default: 5, min: 1, max: 20, step: 1, animate: false },
};
```

See [The module API](/graphics/module-api/) or **Help ▸ Graphics Reference**.

## Values and the module

Each value in an action is checked against the module as it is now, including any minimum and maximum. That has a few effects when the module changes after you've animated it:

- A value already stored isn't checked again, so narrowing a range later leaves the old end value in place.
- If an action names a property the module no longer declares, or no longer lets animate, the row shows dimmed with **⌫**. Choose it to take the property out of the action.
- While the module is missing or won't compile, the **Properties** section has no rows to edit, and reads "The module did not compile — see Source. Stored values are listed below." You can still take values out of the action with **⌫**.

## The badge

The **Graphic** sub-tab shows a **◆N** badge counting how many properties the selected action animates. The **Properties** section header shows the same count. See [Read the sections and sub-tabs](/motion/edit-an-action/#read-the-sections-and-sub-tabs).

## With an agent

An agent works the same way, adding an action and then naming the end values with `set_action_end`. It can't set a value on a property marked `animate: false` that way, and sets it on the clip with `set_graphic` instead. See [Tools: animation](/mcp/tools-animation/).

## Related

- [Actions](/motion/actions/)
- [Set what an action animates to](/motion/edit-an-action/)
- [What an action can animate](/motion/what-can-animate/)
- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Graphic size and timing](/graphics/size-and-timing/)

---
title: "Paste Graphic Properties"
description: Copy the text, colours and other properties of one graphic clip onto other clips drawn by the same graphic, and see what stays behind.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

Paste Graphic Properties copies what one graphic clip shows, its text and colours included, onto other clips drawn by the same graphic. Use it to give a run of lower thirds the same styling, then change the names.

<AtAGlance
  menu="Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties"
  tools="paste_attributes"
/>

## Paste graphic properties

<Steps>

1. Select the graphic clip you want to copy from and press <kbd>⌘C</kbd>.

2. Select the clips to paste onto.

3. Choose **Edit ▸ Paste Graphic Properties**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

</Steps>

Every selected clip drawn by the same graphic takes the copied properties, as one undo step. The menu item is on when there are Frame Job clips on the clipboard and at least one graphic clip is selected.

## What moves and what stays

The target ends up with exactly the copied clip's properties, so a property left at its default on the copied clip goes back to the default on the target.

Each target keeps:

- Its own module, size, **In** and **Length**.
- Its position, scale and everything else outside the **Properties** section.
- Any property the copied clip leaves unset and an action on the target animates, so that the action keeps its start.

If you copied several clips, only the earliest one is read.

## When it does nothing

| What you'll see | Why |
| --- | --- |
| Some selected clips don't change | They're drawn by another graphic, or they aren't graphics. They're skipped. |
| A beep | The copied clip isn't a graphic, no selected clip is drawn by the same graphic, or the targets already match. |
| An alert | The copied properties can't be stored, for example more than 64 of them. It gives the reason, and nothing changes. |

## How it differs from Paste Attributes

**Edit ▸ Paste Attributes** (<kbd>⌥⌘V</kbd>) copies a clip's look, such as its position and opacity, and never carries graphic properties. The two are separate on purpose, because a graphic's properties hold its words as well as its look.

| | Paste Attributes | Paste Graphic Properties |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Position, scale, opacity and other picture settings | Yes | No |
| A graphic's text, colours and other properties | No | Yes |

See [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/).

## Copying a graphic clip

Copying and pasting a graphic clip (<kbd>⌘C</kbd>, <kbd>⌘V</kbd>) pastes a clip that names its module. The module's `.js` file, fonts and pictures are not copied.

So in another project without that module, the pasted clip draws the red error card. To fix it, add the module under the same name, for example with **From File…** in **Insert ▸ Graphic…** on a file of that name. **From File…** also places a clip of its own, which you can delete.

See [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/).

## With an agent

An agent uses `paste_attributes` and has to ask for the graphic group by name, since it's never part of the default set. Unlike the menu item, a clip drawn by another graphic stops the paste with an error, unless the agent asks to skip those. See [Tools: copying and nesting](/mcp/tools-copy-and-nest/).

## Related

- [Paste Attributes](/editing/paste-attributes/)
- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Copy, cut and paste](/editing/copy-and-paste/)

---
title: "Fonts and pictures in graphics"
description: Add fonts and pictures to a project's graphics, find the exact font name a graphic must use, and see why a font or picture doesn't draw.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';

A graphic draws only with the fonts bundled with Frame Job and the fonts and pictures you add to the project, so it looks the same on any Mac. This page covers adding them, and what to do when one doesn't draw.

<AtAGlance
  menu={['File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…', 'File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…']}
  tools={['import_graphic_font', 'import_graphic_asset', 'get_graphic']}
/>

## Add a font

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Font to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. Pick a `.ttf` or `.otf` file.

</Steps>

Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/fonts/` folder, and every graphic in the project can then use it, straight away. Nothing is shown when it works.

A file with the same name replaces the old one. If the file holds no font Frame Job can load, an alert says so and nothing is added.

## Use the exact family name

The family name a graphic must use is the one the graphics engine reads from the file. It can differ from the name Font Book or other apps show.

If a font doesn't draw, select the clip and open **Source** in the **Graphic** sub-tab. Under "Checked at the clip's first frame" it reports the missing family and lists every family the project has, so you can copy the exact name from there. The section's header shows "1 warning" when there's something to read.

The check looks at the clip's first frame only, so a font used later in the animation isn't reported there.

## Bundled fonts

These seven families draw on every Mac, with nothing to install.

| Family | Weights |
| --- | --- |
| Anton | 400 |
| Bebas Neue | 400 |
| Darker Grotesque | Variable, 300 to 900 |
| IBM Plex Mono | 400, 500 |
| Montserrat | 800, 900 |
| Source Sans 3 | Variable, 200 to 900 |
| Source Serif 4 | Variable, 200 to 900 |

## Generic families

A module can also ask for a generic family, which draws in a bundled face.

| Generic | Draws in |
| --- | --- |
| `serif` | Source Serif 4 |
| `sans-serif` | Source Sans 3 |
| `monospace` | IBM Plex Mono |

Write a generic without quotes, as in `font-family="sans-serif"`. With quotes it names a family called "sans-serif", which isn't there. `cursive` and `fantasy` aren't available.

## System fonts

Graphics never use the fonts installed on your Mac, so a project draws the same everywhere. To use one of them, add its file to the project with [Add Font to Graphics](#add-a-font).

What happens to a family name in a module:

- A family the project doesn't have draws nothing, with a warning naming the families it does have.
- In a list such as `"Nope, Montserrat"`, the first family the project has draws.
- A family with a word starting with a digit must be quoted, as in `font-family="'Source Sans 3'"`. Unquoted, it draws nothing, with a warning.

:::note
[Text clips](/text-and-shapes/fonts/) work differently, and do use the fonts on your Mac.
:::

## Add a picture

<Steps>

1. Choose **File ▸ Add Image to Graphics…**. It has no keyboard shortcut.

2. Pick a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, SVG or SVGZ file.

</Steps>

Frame Job copies the file into the project's `graphics/assets/` folder. A module can then draw it, and a [picture property's](/graphics/properties/) pop-up lists it.

A file with the same name replaces the old one. An empty file is refused with an alert, and so is any other kind of file.

## Picture names

A module refers to a picture by its file name, and some names can't be used that way. A name is not usable when it:

- Starts with `.` or `#`.
- Holds any of `/ : " ' < > &`, or a control character.
- Is longer than 247 bytes.

A picture with a name like that is added under a legal one, and a notice tells you which: "#logo&mark.png" was added as "logo-mark.png": asset(name) cannot use the name it had.

If the legal name is taken, the picture takes `-2`, `-3` and so on, as in `logo-mark-2.png`. A renamed copy never replaces an existing file.

## Drop files in the folder

You can also put fonts and pictures straight into `graphics/fonts/` and `graphics/assets/` with the Finder or any other tool. Frame Job notices within a moment.

To find the folder, choose **Reveal in Finder** in the **Source** section of a graphic clip. It shows the module's file inside `graphics/`. If `fonts` or `assets` isn't there yet, make a folder with exactly that name.

Anything the folder scan can't use is skipped, with a warning in **Source** under "In the graphics folder":

- A font that doesn't load.
- An empty picture.
- A picture with a name a module can't use. Unlike a picture added from the menu, it isn't renamed for you.

## Good to know

- Neither import is an undo step. To take a file out, delete it from the folder.
- Fonts and pictures belong to the project. Another project needs its own copy.
- Both menu items work as soon as the project window is open. There's no need to save first.

## With an agent

An agent can read the exact family names directly, rather than waiting for a warning. `get_graphic` lists them, and `import_graphic_font` answers with the names a new file adds. See [Tools: graphic fonts, pictures and packages](/mcp/tools-graphic-files/).

## Related

- [Graphic properties](/graphics/properties/)
- [Write a graphic module](/graphics/write-a-module/)
- [The module API](/graphics/module-api/)
- [Fonts](/text-and-shapes/fonts/)

<system-reminder>
Contents of /Users/kevingalligan/devel/framejob/.claude/worktrees/help-docs/docs/site/CLAUDE.md:

# CLAUDE.md — the documentation site

The public user documentation: Astro with Starlight, one page per feature or tight family of
features. `pnpm` manages it, Node is pinned by `.node-version`. `README.md` has the commands.

## Where things are

```
astro.config.mjs        Starlight's settings: title, logo, fonts, theme, plugins
sidebar.mjs             every page's place in the navigation, in order
src/content/docs/       the pages: <section>/<page>.mdx
src/data/features.json  THE FEATURE LIST: what /features/ renders and what the proof reads
src/components/         AtAGlance (a page's facts), Shot (a screen in both looks),
                        FeatureIndex (the filterable list)
src/assets/screens/     WebP captures, written only by scripts/import-screens.mjs
src/styles/             the brand: the mark's inks, the app's faces, square chrome
```

## The rule that matters

**Every claim is written from the code.** A label, a default, a range, a shortcut, a limit or a
refusal is checked against `app/Sources/`, `core/src/`, `graphic/` or `mcp-proxy/` before it is
written, and the code wins over `docs/guide/`, a spec or an ADR. Never write what a feature
probably does. If the code cannot settle it, leave it out.

Nothing dev-only, deferred or unbuilt is documented. That excludes the dev tools (`snapshot_ui`,
`perform_menu_item`, `cancel_sheet`, `select_inspector_tab`, `play_preview`, `graphic_memory`,
`loudness_meter`, `land_recording`, `analysis_job`, `transcript_view`, `playback_rebuilds`,
`assistant_send`, `assistant_answer`) and every `-RCDev` launch default.

## Who reads this

Someone editing a video, who has never read this repository. They want to know what a thing does,
how to do it, and what will stop them. They do not care how it is built.

So a page never mentions: spec or decision IDs (`AU-12`, `§11`), road maps, phases, issue numbers,
source file or type names, `rc_*` exports, format version numbers, proofs, tests, or the history
of a feature. Internal words get translated: "refused" becomes what the user sees ("Frame Job
won't do this while…"), "the core" and "the op" disappear. A tool name is the one exception: the
MCP pages and `tools=` in `AtAGlance` name agent tools, because those are the product's interface.

## Voice

- Plain, direct and second person. Say what it does, then how. Short sentences.
- Open with what the feature is for, in a sentence or two, before any steps.
- British spelling in prose, as `docs/guide/` does (colour, centre, grey, normalise), and the
  app's exact spelling for its own labels (the **Color** tab, **Normalize**).
- Contractions are fine. No marketing: never "powerful", "seamless", "effortless", "robust",
  "simply", "just", "easily", "unleash", "supercharge".
- Prefer a full stop or a comma to an em dash.
- State defaults, ranges and limits as numbers. Say what happens at the edges, because that is
  what a reader comes to a reference for.
- No filler sections. A page with nothing to say under a heading doesn't have that heading.

## Page shape

```mdx
---
title: Markers
description: One sentence, what this page helps you do. Search results show it.
---

import { Steps } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';
import AtAGlance from '@components/AtAGlance.astro';
import Shot from '@components/Shot.astro';

What the feature is for, in a sentence or two.

<AtAGlance menu="Mark ▸ Add Marker" keys="M" tools="add_marker" />

<Shot name="04-editor.window" alt="What the picture shows, for someone who can't see it." />

## Add a marker

<Steps>

1. Move the playhead to the moment.
2. Press <kbd>M</kbd>.

</Steps>

## Options

| Control | What it does | Default |
| ------- | ------------ | ------- |

## Good to know

Limits, edge cases and what stops it, in plain words.

## Related

- [Snapping](/timeline/snapping/)
```

Every section is optional except the opening. Order the task sections as a reader needs them.

- **Headings** start at `##`, are sentence case, and name the job: "Add a marker", not "Adding".
  A feature in `src/data/features.json` with an `anchor` needs a heading that makes that anchor.
- **Menus** are bold with `▸`, spelled as the app spells them: **Clip ▸ Split**.
- **Keys** use the app's symbols in `<kbd>`: <kbd>⌘T</kbd>. Inside `AtAGlance`, pass the string.
- **Controls** are bold where they appear in a step: choose **Save**.
- **Links** are root-absolute with a trailing slash: `/timeline/markers/#add-a-marker`. The build
  fails on a link or anchor that does not exist.
- **Asides** are for what a reader must not miss, not for decoration: `:::note`, `:::tip`,
  `:::caution`, `:::danger`.
- **Screens** come from `src/assets/screens/`. A `name` is the file name without its look and
  extension. Use a screen only when it shows what the page is about, not when the thing is out
  of frame, and give it real alt text.

## MDX traps

MDX is JSX. In prose, `{`, `}` and `<` start code. Put anything like `{x}`, `<1 s` or `a<b` in a
code span, or write it out ("under 1 s"). `<kbd>` and every component must close. A line starting
with `import` or `export` is code. Leave a blank line after an opening component tag and before
its closing tag, or the Markdown inside won't render.

## Checking a page

```sh
node docs/site/scripts/check-pages.mjs <page.mdx>…        # parses, imports, links, captures
python3 tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py --pages <page.mdx>…  # internal words, local paths
pnpm build                                                # in docs/site: the last word
```

## Screens

The captures come from the screen catalog (`designs/screens/`, `tools/proof/screens.py`), so the
pictures are of the real app. To refresh them:

```sh
python3 tools/proof/screens.py --out <dir>                      # from the repository root
node docs/site/scripts/import-screens.mjs <dir> --used
```

**This site is public.** `import-screens.mjs` refuses a capture whose layout dump holds a local
path, and its `CROP` table is the only way past that, by cutting the region away. Settings needs
it: its MCP section prints the helper's full path. Never weaken the refusal.

## When the app changes

A user-visible change edits its page here as well as `docs/guide/`, and a new feature adds its row
to `src/data/features.json`. `tools/proof/docs_site_proof.py` runs in `make test` and fails on a
menu item or agent tool the site doesn't document, a feature whose page or anchor is missing, or a
page that names something internal.

</system-reminder>
